newsitem.title: UK: LIMIT says Bankside offer unconditional.
newsitem.headline: LIMIT says Bankside offer unconditional.

text.p: Lloyd's of London's largest corporate investor LIMIT (London Insurance Market Investmewnt Trust) said on Tuesday that its offer for 65 percent of Bankside Underwriting Agencies Limited had been accepted by shareholders.

LIMIT also announced that its total underwriting capacity at Lloyd's for 1997 had risen 2.1 percent to 643.8 million stg and that it had allocated capacity to 84 syndicates compared with 95 last year.
Bankside is the second leading managing agency at Lloyd's that LIMIT has taken a majority interest in over the past three months.

In October the group announced the 18.6 million stg takeover of managing agent Janson Green and the group has made additional investments in five other Lloyd's dedicated capital providers and managing agencies.

Bankside has underwriting capacity of about 422 million pounds in 1997 and also owns Garwyn Limited, a loss adjusting business. The acquisition was carried out by a LIMIT subsidiary, renamed Bankside Insurance Holdings Plc, which the company eventually plans to float on the London Stock Exchange.
At December 31 LIMIT said the net tangible asset value per share was 120.4 pence.

Despite more competitive trading conditions it said it hoped that the 1997 underwriting account would produce a small positive return and Chairman Jonathan Agnew said the group was "well placed in the changing Lloyd's market".
